statement: Define $a_{1}=\\sqrt{2}$ and $a_{n+1}=\\sqrt{2+a_{n}}$ for $n\\ge1$. Show by induction that $a_{n}<2$ for all $n$, that the sequence is increasing, and hence find $\\lim_{n\\to\\infty}a_{n}$.
solution: Boundedness: $a_{1}=\\sqrt{2}<2$. If $a_{n}<2$ then $a_{n+1}=\\sqrt{2+a_{n}}<\\sqrt{4}=2$, so by induction $a_{n}<2$ for all $n$. Monotonicity: $a_{n+1}^{2}-a_{n}^{2}=2+a_{n}-a_{n}^{2}=(2-a_{n})(1+a_{n})$. Since $0<a_{n}<2$, both factors are positive, so $a_{n+1}^{2}>a_{n}^{2}$ and thus $a_{n+1}>a_{n}$. The sequence is increasing and bounded above by $2$, so it converges to some limit $L$. Then $L=\\sqrt{2+L}$, i.e. $L^{2}-L-2=0$, giving $L=2$ (the positive root). Thus $\\lim_{n\\to\\infty}a_{n}=2$.
hints: Compare a_{n+1}^2 and a_n^2 to show increase.
Let the limit be L and solve L=sqrt(2+L).
